extracted.intended_audience: internal communicators, team leads, corporate writers, and organizations who draft email/Slack/Teams/SharePoint updates
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing concise, high-impact internal communications using the Smart Brevity formula (headlines, 'why it matters', formatting, and structure) so busy readers quickly understand and act. Includes examples, training, and a checklist to implement the method across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate what matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity is a communication methodology used to communicate what matters to staff and stakeholders more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the most important information for staff and stakeholders; trim ancillary detail. The methodology exists to help readers 'easily absorb and act on what they read.' Avoid including background or praise that doesn't change decisions or actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with 'What's new' and 'Why it matters'
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell readers 'What's new' and 'Why it matters' first — always — so they stick with us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a clear 'what's new' statement and an immediate 'why it matters' explanation. Example structure in the after version: '1 big thing: We wowed our Board' followed by a short 'Why it matters' paragraph. Anti-pattern: burying news and relevance deep in long paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the reader's two instant questions
rubrics_metrics.description: When we see new content — our brains ask two things: What is this about? Is this relevant to me? If we can't get to 'yes' in about 17 milliseconds, we move on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the very first lines make clear the topic and the audience-relevant reason to continue. Design subject lines/headlines and lead sentences so readers can decide within milliseconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use one-big-thing headline and concise substructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a clear single takeaway (e.g., '1 big thing: We wowed our Board') and follow with short labeled sections like 'Why it matters', 'How we did it', 'What's next'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize messages into a small set of labeled short sections (big thing, why it matters, key bullets, next steps). The sample after-message shows practical labels: '1 big thing', 'Why it matters', 'New hires', 'Partnerships', 'How we did it', 'What's next.' This keeps readers focused on the main point and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break up text visually (white space, bolding, images, bullets)
rubrics_metrics.description: There's a winning mix of white space, bolding, images and bullets that will break us out of that haze.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid big blocks of text which cause readers to 'zone out.' Use white space, bolding for emphasis, bullets for lists, and images where helpful to improve scannability. The before example is a cautionary anti-pattern: long dense paragraphs that lose readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep communications brief and reduce read time
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity produces 40% shorter read times, on average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to shorten content significantly — cut unnecessary words and digressions. Use concise sentences and prioritize content that supports the main takeaway. The after example demonstrates drastically shorter, punchier copy vs. the long 'Before' version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform complex messages into high-impact communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainers help you discover how to transform complex messages into high-impact communications and learn tested, proven methods for arranging, formatting, and styling effective communication—using real examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify and prioritize complex information so the core message is immediately actionable. Use tested arranging and styling techniques demonstrated in examples or training to preserve necessary nuance while maintaining brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use data- and brain-science-informed techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity® powers clear communication — a formula based on brain science and data that helps you style and format information to be clear, engaging and memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design messages informed by reader attention limits (e.g., 26-second average read, 17 ms initial decision). Prefer formats and phrasing shown by testing to increase engagement and recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the method across channels and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity works for any form of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same principles for email, Slack, Teams, SharePoint updates, and other formats — adapting labels and length to channel norms. The product supports planning, drafting, collaborating, sending, tracking, and optimizing across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the checklist, examples, and training to implement the style
rubrics_metrics.description: Smart Brevity Checklist: This checklist helps you remember the key ingredients of Smart Brevity so your next communication is clearer, more engaging, and memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the checklist and attend trainings or webinars to learn the muscle of Smart Brevity. Use before/after samples and the provided checklist to audit drafts and ensure communications conform to the method.
